prompt: A particle moves along a line with position $s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t$ for $t \ge 0$. During which time interval is the particle moving to the LEFT (in the negative direction)?
hint: Moving left means velocity is negative. Find $v(t) = s'(t)$ and factor it.

hints.text: Moving left means velocity is negative. Find $v(t) = s'(t)$ and factor it.
Between the roots: $1 < t < 3$. Choice B.

explanation: The product of two factors is negative exactly when they have opposite signs: $t - 1 > 0$ and $t - 3 < 0$, i.e. $1 < t < 3$.
So the particle moves left from $t = 1$ to $t = 3$. It turns around at both of those instants: $s(1) = 4$ and $s(3) = 0$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test a time in each region
steps: $v(4) = 3(3)(1) = 9 > 0$: moving right again. Only $(1, 3)$ is a leftward stretch.
